stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The two department heads will discuss about the budget during the meeting.
hints: Some verbs take their object directly, with no small word in between.
Read the verb and what follows: "discuss about the budget". Try it without "about".

Some verbs take their object directly, with no preposition in between: you attend a meeting, enter a room, reach a decision. Ask whether the verb in this sentence is one of them, then check each part.

steps.action: Look at the verb "discuss" and the word after it: "about".
"Discuss" already means "talk about", so it takes its object directly: "discuss the budget".
Check the other parts. "The two department heads" and "during the meeting" are correct.
The error is "will discuss about". It should be "will discuss".

trapNotes.The two department heads: This part is correct. It names who will do the talking.
trapNotes.during the meeting: This part is correct. "During" is the right word for something that happens within an event.
trapNotes.No error: We say "talk about" and "a discussion about", so "discuss about" may sound right. But the verb "discuss" takes no "about": you discuss the budget.
